content.comment_body: Hello, I recently purchased a [product_name] with relay outputs, which I am operating at 115V AC. I need to connect 115V contactors to the outputs of the [product_name], but I am unsure about the correct wiring approach. Should there be a dedicated automatic circuit-breaker for the [product_name] power supply, and a separate one for the outputs? Or is it acceptable to protect both the power supply and outputs using a single circuit breaker? I would appreciate any advice on this issue. Thank you!

If you are supplying the [product_name] from the same power source, it is possible to use just one circuit breaker. However, please note that the maximum for the extension contacts is 4A, so you typically do not need much power. I recommend using a 2A fuse or automatic circuit breaker. For troubleshooting, it can sometimes be better to use separate circuit breakers, such as: - [product_name] Power (F1A) - [product_name] input circuit (F1A) - [product_name] output circuit (T2A) I usually use fuseholders (and accessories) like: [url]
Thank you [user_name], your response was very helpful!
